subject: Lifecare: subprocessor appointment, bridge letter & TIA scoping
messages:
From: Sue Huang <sue.huang@lifecare.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: privacy@lifecare.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: proof of subprocessor appointment + TIA scoping

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for the DPA draft — attached are our redlines (see redlines_lifecare_dpa_v3.pdf). Before we loop legal in for signoff there are two operational items we need clarified so our data protection team can complete the TIA:

1) Subprocessor appointment evidence: can you provide a dated CSV/list of active subprocessors with the following columns: name, role, country of processing, evidence of appointment (contract or deed), and data categories processed. We usually require this as proof for our procurement and TIA.

2) Bridge letter / fallback controls: because we will be routing certain patient-data flows through EU and non-EU providers during a phased rollout, we need an interim bridge-letter style assurance or a concise summary of technical safeguards (encryption at-rest/in-transit, access controls, logging, and retention exception handling) until the UK IDTA and SCC mapping is finalized.

Can you confirm ETA for those two items? Also indicate if any subprocessors are onshore-only vs. multi-region.

Thanks — Sue
Sue Huang
Senior Privacy Counsel, Lifecare Inc.
Attachment: Lifecare_redlines.zip (contains redlines_lifecare_dpa_v3.pdf)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sue Huang <sue.huang@lifecare.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: proof of subprocessor appointment + TIA scoping

Hi Sue — thanks for the clear notes and the redlines. We're on it. Quick plan and asks from our side:

- Subprocessor CSV: we can provide an exported CSV that matches your columns. Preliminary ETA: 48 business hours (EOD Fri 21 Aug) for the full list and current appointment artifacts.
- Bridge letter / interim safeguards: we don't issue legal "bridge letters" as a matter of course, but we will produce a concise technical assurance memo that contains:
  * encryption and key custody (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit; KMS in EU for EU-resident workloads),
  * access controls and MFA on operator consoles,
  * audit logging/retention windows and log export process, and
  * fallback routing & model-variant policy for cross-border handling during phased rollout.
  ETA for memo: EOD Mon 24 Aug (we can compress if necessary).

Internal: Kim, can you confirm whether the KMS keys for Lifecare's EU workloads are in eu-west-1 and whether we can include the audit log retention export as an evidence artifact? Jon, I'll need you to sign the attestation once the CSV is assembled so we can provide a hand-signed subprocessor list for procurement.

Sue — are there any specific format constraints for the evidence CSV? If you attach a small sample of the exact csv headings you require we'll mirror it.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: -- none --

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, Sue Huang <sue.huang@lifecare.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: proof of subprocessor appointment + TIA scoping

Olga / Sue — quick technical confirmations to feed the memo and CSV:

- KMS & key residency: Lifecare EU tenant is configured to use customer-managed keys located in eu-west-1. We maintain separate key aliases per-customer; control plane key metadata will be included in the memo (no private key material).
- Audit logs: infra and runtime logs are retained for 90 days in our core observability cluster, and we can produce a signed, timestamped export (CSV) of access events for a 30-day window to support your TIA checklist. That export will include: timestamp, actor, action, resource, region, and request id.
- Subprocessors: current active subprocessors (high-level):
  * Cloud infra provider A (eu-west-1) — infra + storage
  * Model accelerators provider X (multi-region; eu and us) — dedicated inference hardware (no long-term storage)
  * Managed logging partner L — log aggregation and short-term indexing (eu region instances available)
  Full CSV will include per-row links to appointment artifacts (contract id) where available.

Attachments (for tech review): service_boundary_diagram.png, subprocessor_attestation_20260820.csv (redacted sample).

I can shorten the memo timeline if Lifecare needs it by EOD Mon; otherwise target Mon EOD per Olga's note.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: service_boundary_diagram.png (image), subprocessor_attestation_20260820.csv (csv)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sue Huang <sue.huang@lifecare.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: proof of subprocessor appointment + TIA scoping

Hi all — following up with deliverables and next steps.

Deliverables attached to this thread:
- redlines_lifecare_dpa_v3.pdf (copied back into thread for completeness)
- subprocessor_attestation_20260820.csv (full export; redacted PII)
- service_boundary_diagram.png

Actions we completed:
1) Olga assembled the CSV and I have signed the attestation (signature page will be included in the HubSpot record).
2) Kim prepared the technical assurance memo draft (stored in Drive link below).
3) Procurement-friendly artifact: we created a one-page "bridge assurance summary" that maps the interim safeguards to each data category; that is intended to be a stop-gap for your procurement / TIA reviewers.

Next steps for Lifecare: please confirm acceptance of the CSV format and whether the bridge assurance summary is sufficient to move the TIA to the next phase. If you prefer a Bridge Letter in legal wording, we can propose a short-form clause for your counsel to take to Lifecare legal — that will require legal review on our side and may add 3-5 business days.

DocuSign and records: once you confirm, I'll raise a DocuSign request for the DPA redlines versus our counter and add the signed attestation as an exhibit. Draft sign path: Lifecare Legal -> Redwood Legal -> Redwood Operations.

Drive link to memo and artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/TIA-Lifecare-2026
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/records/companies/LC-4821

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
